title: Conditional ordered-limit rectangular-tail bridge
question: Can explicit uniform cutoff and volume tail bounds be composed in either declared order into one common rectangular-tail estimate before an owner-specific ordered limit is claimed?

theorem.cutoff_then_volume: If |A(n,m)-B(m)|<epsilon/2 for all n>=N and all m, and |B(m)-L|<epsilon/2 for all m>=M, then |A(n,m)-L|<epsilon for n>=N,m>=M.
theorem.volume_then_cutoff: If |A(n,m)-C(n)|<epsilon/2 for all m>=M and all n, and |C(n)-L|<epsilon/2 for all n>=N, then |A(n,m)-L|<epsilon for n>=N,m>=M.
theorem.order_contract: The two orders are separate owner obligations; agreement of their rectangular tails is a compatibility check, not a proof of existence of either physical limit.
theorem.norm_contract: The absolute value is a placeholder for the common norm selected by the source owner; replacing it by an operator or field norm requires a separate domain theorem.

model.indices: n=cutoff or lattice index, m=volume or exhaustion index

assumptions: The triangle inequality is applied in one already declared common norm.
The cutoff and volume tails are supplied with strict epsilon/2 bounds before the rectangle is formed.
The two parameter indices and their order are fixed before any fitting or limit interpretation.
The finite fixture is an arithmetic self-test of the contract and is not an owner packet or exhaustion surrogate.
missing_assumptions: A hash-pinned source-owned TECT functional and compatible generator or transfer.
A common invariant core and norm for all regulated observables.
Source-authorized cutoff- and volume-uniform bounds, including boundary and phase dependence.
A proof that the specified A, B and C objects are the same physical observable across regulators.
An ordered removal rule for cutoff, lattice, volume, exhaustion, phase and beta, plus existence or equivalence-class language.
Physical-sector projection and an independent holdout observation map.
non_claims: No source-owned dynamics or production owner is supplied.
No actual Q3 common core, uniform estimate, thermodynamic limit, continuum limit or common-alpha theorem is proved.
The synthetic geometric fixture does not represent the TECT field law and cannot close Pre-A, Sector-A, QFT, Yang--Mills, gravity or mass gap.
The two orders are not inferred to agree merely because both fixture calculations pass.

adversarial_review.check: A strict epsilon/2 split is required before adding the two tails.
adversarial_review.disposition: UPHELD by Lean and both arithmetic lanes.

adversarial_review.check: The forward and reverse intermediate functions are not silently swapped.
adversarial_review.disposition: UPHELD by explicit order labels and hostile mutation rejection.

adversarial_review.check: A finite sample must not be relabelled as a uniform owner bound.
adversarial_review.disposition: UPHELD-OPEN; fixture rows are fenced as arithmetic only.

adversarial_review.check: Absolute-value bookkeeping must not be promoted to an operator-domain theorem.
adversarial_review.disposition: UPHELD-OPEN; common norm and domain remain missing.

adversarial_review.check: A rectangular tail must not close the physical sector or QFT identity.

lean.role: Lean checks only the epsilon-split triangle implications; it does not formalise TECT operators, domains, source ownership or limits.

evidence_level: T0 exact conditional two-order epsilon bridge with independent and hostile checks
boundary: R-474 closes only the abstract epsilon bookkeeping needed to turn owner-supplied uniform tails into a rectangular-tail certificate. It does not supply those tails or any source-owned TECT input.
next_action: When a non-synthetic owner packet arrives, instantiate both order contracts in the declared common norm and test source-, cutoff-, volume-, lattice-, phase- and beta-uniformity before attempting the ordered limit; until then keep T-054 at owner intake and do not repeat finite physical-empty tests.
